correctness.summary: The categorical construction checks term by term. Additivity of the Euler class makes A_phi extension closed, split complements remain in A_phi, and standard cone conflations retain enough projective-injectives. Semisimplicity splits bounded complexes into cohomology stalks plus a contractible summand, which justifies I=<F> and J=<C>. The displayed Ext^1 decomposition gives the ideal orthogonality, and multiplying test stalks by the exponent e puts them back in A_phi. The explicit special ideal precover and preenvelope have kernel/cokernel multiplied by e, so their Euler obstruction vanishes. Conversely, the two-stalk objects force a nonzero Euler class in any putative special object approximation, proving failure of object completeness. Finally X^e lies in A_phi for every ambient complex X, while a one-copy summand need not, proving the stated idempotent-completion result.

limitations: The motivating parity paper is extremely recent, so concurrent generalizations remain a realistic originality risk.
The construction uses semisimplicity essentially in the cohomology splitting and explicit Ext formula.
Classical K0/dense-subcategory machinery is prior art and is not treated as new.

originality.summary: Ren-Wang's September 2026 preprint gives the modulus-two vector-space parity example, while Matsui and Thomason supply classical Grothendieck-group descriptions of dense subcategories. Searches did not locate the stated finite-K0-quotient cotorsion theorem. The contribution is therefore best described as a natural but nontrivial finite-quotient generalization of a very recent counterexample, not as novelty of the dense-subcategory mechanism itself.

scientific_value.summary: Replacing parity by an arbitrary nonzero finite quotient isolates the extension-stable invariant responsible for the counterexample and gives explicit approximation sequences uniformly across semisimple finite-length categories. This turns a single example into a reusable structural mechanism.
